title: StarRocks chaos: kill a BE; queries reroute, tablets re-replicate
description: The nexus-cli chaos verb for StarRocks: stop a BE and verify queries still return full results (replication_num=3 means every tablet has a replica on a surviving BE), then restart and watch the FE re-balance/re-replicate.

steps.command: ssh -i $NEXUS_SSH_KEY nexusadmin@192.168.70.31 "mysql --skip-ssl -h 127.0.0.1 -P 9030 -u root -p$SR_ROOT_PW -N -e 'SELECT count(*) FROM nexus.events'"

observe.what: sr-be-1 shows Alive=false; the FE marks its tablets unavailable on that BE but each has replicas on the other 2

steps.command: ssh -i $NEXUS_SSH_KEY nexusadmin@192.168.70.31 "mysql --skip-ssl -h 127.0.0.1 -P 9030 -u root -p$SR_ROOT_PW -N -e 'SELECT count(*) FROM nexus.events'"

observe.what: same count as baseline -- the query reroutes to surviving tablet replicas (no data unavailability with replication_num=3)
sr-be-1 returns Alive=true; the FE tablet scheduler re-balances/re-replicates as needed

whatProves: a BE loss does not make any tablet unavailable -- queries reroute to surviving replicas (replication_num=3) -- and the BE auto-recovers + re-balances on restart. Replication across BE is real.
